question: A serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) of ≥1.1 g/dL indicates that ascites is caused by portal hypertension.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL is the validated threshold for portal hypertension-related ascites with >97% accuracy. Remember: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic fluid albumin, both measured on the same day.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL has >97% accuracy for diagnosing portal hypertension-related ascites (cirrhosis, cardiac failure, Budd-Chiari). SAAG <1.1 g/dL points to non-portal-hypertensive causes such as malignancy, TB peritonitis, or nephrotic syndrome.
